newsitem.title: FRANCE: French pensions bill adopted by parliament.
newsitem.headline: French pensions bill adopted by parliament.

text.p: A bill introducing private pensions to France was definitively adopted by parliament on Thursday and the bills's author said the first funds could be up and running before the end of the year.

Both the Senate, the upper house, and the National Assembly, the lower house adopted the final text and Jean-Pierre Thomas, the bill's author, said the decrees applying the legislation would to be adopted before the summer.

"The decrees will be adopted before the summer. Negotiations between employers and employees can start from the summer and the first pension funds set up from autumn. In any case, we will have the first funds before the end of the year," Thomas told journalists.
Thomas also said he expected the funds to attract 20 to 30 billion francs a year once the system reached "cruising speed."
The opposition Socialists had objected to the pensions bill on the grounds it could drain away money from the existing pay-as-you-go state-backed pensions scheme.

However a socialist party source toned down earlier claims that the law would be repealed if the socialists came to power. He said the law would be hard to repeal but that certain clauses could be changed.
The pensions fund bill will give about 14 million private sector employees the option to save for their own retirment and employers will be allowed to top up workers' contributions if they wish.

The main opposition to the bill centred on a clause which gives employers incentives, including exemptions from social security charges, to pay in money on behalf of staff. Employers will be allowed to pay in up to four times staff contributions.
The Socialists, Communists and all the main trade unions have said this would lead to money being drained away from the social security funds which finance the basic state-pension system.

One of the main aims of the bill is to channel investment into the French stock market. One of the measures in the bill is a cap limiting any fund's investment in bonds, currently the favoured investment instrument in France, to 60 percent of stocks. (( -- William Emmanuel, Paris Newsroom +331 4221 5452))
